checks.title: Energy: the closed domain keeps it
checks.registered: 2026-09-29, before the acoustics family's first run
checks.measure: max over steps of |E_n - E_0| / E_0, E the leapfrog's own energy sum rho_f v^2/2 + sum p_n p_(n+1) / (2 K), worst arm
checks.why: leapfrog conserves that quantity exactly on a closed domain, so what is left is the round-off of the updates and the sums, about 1e-16 per step over a few thousand steps

checks.title: Reflection = (Z2 - Z1) / (Z2 + Z1)
checks.registered: 2026-09-29, before the acoustics family's first run
checks.measure: max over the steps when the reflected pulse is alone in the first medium of |sum of p there / sum of p of the incident pulse - R|, R the textbook normal-incidence reflection with Z = rho c
checks.why: the discrete interface reflects the zero-wavenumber component with R exactly (the module's derivation), and the pulse's integral is that component; what is left is the Gaussian's tail beyond the seven-width margin (about 2e-11) and round-off. 1e-6 leaves room for what the derivation did not see
checks.detail: R measured 0.999443938429 (mean over steps 1021-2000; largest departure 3.1e-10), textbook 0.999443938429

checks.title: The two pieces equal the full domain, bit for bit
checks.registered: 2026-09-29, before the acoustics family's first run
checks.measure: np.array_equal on the pressure and both velocities after every step
checks.why: every face and cell is updated from the same numbers by the same arithmetic in either arm; the exchange only moves the numbers

notes: Leapfrog step 4e-06 s against the stability limit 4.774e-06 s (Gershgorin on the grid's own operator). The pieces trade the pressures beside the interface and its velocities once a step; nothing iterates.

Impedances Z = rho c: 411.6 and 1.48e+06 Pa s/m. Textbook reflection R = 0.999444, transmission T = 1 + R = 1.999444 (the transmitted pressure is 2 times the incident), energy transmitted 1 - R^2 = 0.001112 at zero wavenumber. The energy share the page plots is carried by the pulse's whole spectrum, whose discrete reflection departs from R at order (k dx)^2, so it is close to that and not equal; the reflection check reads the zero-wavenumber part, where the scheme is exact.
The reflected pulse is alone in the first medium from step 1021 to step 2027; the reflection is read there.
